gap: No result ChatGPT got states which 25,000-27,650 mAh banks are in stock at or under $100 at their makers' own US stores on 2026-11-26: eight are, from $59.98 to $99.99, and only two of those state a 140 W port on the store text read; two more get under $100 only with a code (UGREEN Nexode 200W is $129.99 at UGREEN, not the $80 ChatGPT showed), and INIU's 140 W models are sold out at INIU.
standout_why: Compared against dupple.com (cited, dated 2026-11-10), both powerbanks.fyi pages (one cited; prices 'checked Aug 18'), and the UGREEN and INIU collection pages. Dupple already prices the category with $/Wh and a drawback per model, so the idea is not new. Its prices are stale and no-code, though: UGREEN 145W $79.99 (now $59.98), Sharge HyperTower 170 $109.90 (now $75.90), Anker 25K $119.99 (now $91.19). It omits AOHi and treats INIU as invalid listings. Powerbanks.fyi gives no input watts, no codes and no ranking reasons, and shows UGREEN 145W at $109.99. None of them says the $80 Nexode 200W needs a code or that the INIU 140 W models are sold out. If the Baseus FC41 code price ($46.99, last cart-tested 2026-11-18, not re-tested by me) is left out, this drops to 1. TechRadar AU (cited in chat 1) came back truncated, so it was not compared.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's pick at no-code prices: UGREEN 145W 25K at $59.98 is the cheapest in-stock 25,000 mAh bank read today and has a 140 W port. INIU P63, Sharge HyperTower 170, AOHi Black Warrior, Anker 25K and the EcoFlow RAPID cable version all cost more, and each maker's text gives 100 W as its fastest charging figure. EcoFlow RAPID 25K 170W ($85.99) is the only one whose store text states 140 W input, so it wins the fast-recharge segment at $26 more. The pick flips to Baseus EnerFill FC41 25K (built-in cables; 140 W and 65 W input per Dealectric's table) only if code FC41 still gives $46.99 at checkout; at its $79.99 store price it loses to UGREEN by $20. UGREEN Nexode 200W and AOHi Future Starship belong on the page only as 'under $100 with the code' rows.

findings.label: UGREEN US store price
findings.note: Read from UGREEN's store catalogue with storecheck search; the product page itself returned HTTP 429 on later tries. Store text: '140W Charge, 145W MAX, 65W Recharge'. $59.98 / 90 Wh = $0.67 per Wh. Lowest in-stock price of the 25,000-27,650 mAh banks read today at the stores named here. Loses only on recharge speed (65 W in).

findings.label: UGREEN's spec table: capacity, ports, protocols
findings.value: 25,000 mAh / 3.6 V / 90 Wh (TYP); USB-C1 out up to 28 V 5 A, 140 W max; USB-C2 65 W max; USB-A 22.5 W max; USB-C1 input 65 W max
findings.note: This is UGREEN's bundle listing for the same power bank, and the only UGREEN listing whose spec table came through. The image caption says 'PD3.1 140w'. The 'USB-C1/C2 Output Protocols' line reads PD3.0/PD2.0/QC3.0/.../PPS, so UGREEN lists PPS on output but names PD3.0 on that line while also listing 28 V 5 A, a PD 3.1 level. The input-protocol line names PD3.1/PPS. The bundle is $75.98 (list $111.43), in stock.
